title: 1 Samuel 6: The Ark Returned with a Trespass Offering
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Samuel 6](/bible/1-samuel/6)

**[1 Samuel 6:1-6](/bible/1-samuel/6#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/1-samuel/6#v1)</sup> And the ark of the Lord was in the country of the Philistines seven months.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-samuel/6#v2)</sup> And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, What shall we do to the ark of the Lord? tell us wherewith we shall send it to his place.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-samuel/6#v3)</sup> And they said, If ye send away the ark of the God of Israel, send it not empty; but in any wise return him a trespass offering: then ye shall be healed, and it shall be known to you why his hand is not removed from you.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/1-samuel/6#v4)</sup> Then said they, What shall be the trespass offering which we shall return to him? They answered, Five golden emerods, and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines: for one plague was on you all, and on your lords.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-samuel/6#v5)</sup> Wherefore ye shall make images of your emerods, and images of your mice that mar the land; and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel: peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/1-samuel/6#v6)</sup> Wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? when he had wrought wonderfully among them, did they not let the people go, and they departed?

- The ark of the Lord was in the country of the Philistines seven months, and the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, asking how to send it back to his place. Seven months of that plague and they had to get it out of the land.
- The priests answered, send it not empty, but in any wise return him a trespass offering; then ye shall be healed. A trespass offering acknowledges you did wrong. The offering was five golden emerods and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines, images of the very things that marred the land, and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel; peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land.
- Their own priests warned them from Israel's history: wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? They did not want to end up like Egypt, so they said, let us learn the lesson and get this ark back.

**[1 Samuel 6:7-12](/bible/1-samuel/6#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/1-samuel/6#v7)</sup> Now therefore make a new cart, and take two milch kine, on which there hath come no yoke, and tie the kine to the cart, and bring their calves home from them:
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-samuel/6#v8)</sup> And take the ark of the Lord, and lay it upon the cart; and put the jewels of gold, which ye return him for a trespass offering, in a coffer by the side thereof; and send it away, that it may go.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-samuel/6#v9)</sup> And see, if it goeth up by the way of his own coast to Beth–shemesh, then he hath done us this great evil: but if not, then we shall know that it is not his hand that smote us; it was a chance that happened to us.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-samuel/6#v10)</sup> And the men did so; and took two milch kine, and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home:
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-samuel/6#v11)</sup> And they laid the ark of the Lord upon the cart, and the coffer with the mice of gold and the images of their emerods.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-samuel/6#v12)</sup> And the kine took the straight way to the way of Beth–shemesh, and went along the highway, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left; and the lords of the Philistines went after them unto the border of Beth–shemesh.

- The test: make a new cart, take two milch kine on which there hath come no yoke, shut up their calves at home, lay the ark on the cart with the jewels of gold in a coffer, and send it away. If it goeth up by the way of his own coast to Beth-shemesh, then he hath done us this great evil: but if not, we shall know it was a chance that happened to us, maybe just a disease spreading through the nation.
- The kine took the straight way to the way of Beth-shemesh, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left, with the lords of the Philistines following to the border. Cows with no yoke, separated from their calves, walking a straight line home to Israel: that settled that it was the hand of the Lord.

**[1 Samuel 6:13-18](/bible/1-samuel/6#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/1-samuel/6#v13)</sup> And they of Beth–shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley: and they lifted up their eyes, and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-samuel/6#v14)</sup> And the cart came into the field of Joshua, a Beth–shemite, and stood there, where there was a great stone: and they clave the wood of the cart, and offered the kine a burnt offering unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-samuel/6#v15)</sup> And the Levites took down the ark of the Lord, and the coffer that was with it, wherein the jewels of gold were, and put them on the great stone: and the men of Beth–shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices the same day unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-samuel/6#v16)</sup> And when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-samuel/6#v17)</sup> And these are the golden emerods which the Philistines returned for a trespass offering unto the Lord; for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Askelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-samuel/6#v18)</sup> And the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both of fenced cities, and of country villages, even unto the great stone of Abel, whereon they set down the ark of the Lord: which stone remaineth unto this day in the field of Joshua, the Beth–shemite.

- They of Beth-shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley, and when they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, they rejoiced to see it. As soon as the ark crossed that border coming home, it was rejoicing time in Israel.
- The cart came into the field of Joshua, a Beth-shemite, and stood by a great stone; they clave the wood of the cart and offered the kine a burnt offering unto the Lord, and the Levites took down the ark and the coffer with the jewels of gold.
- The golden emerods were one for each lord's city, Ashdod, Gaza, Askelon, Gath, and Ekron, and when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day. The Philistines understood it really was the Lord that had afflicted them.

**[1 Samuel 6:19-21](/bible/1-samuel/6#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/1-samuel/6#v19)</sup> And he smote the men of Beth–shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the Lord, even he smote of the people fifty thousand and threescore and ten men: and the people lamented, because the Lord had smitten many of the people with a great slaughter.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-samuel/6#v20)</sup> And the men of Beth–shemesh said, Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God? and to whom shall he go up from us?
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/1-samuel/6#v21)</sup> And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kirjath–jearim, saying, The Philistines have brought again the ark of the Lord; come ye down, and fetch it up to you.

- He smote the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the Lord, even fifty thousand and threescore and ten men. It was not just the other nations that had to keep discretion with the ark of the covenant; it was forbidden to touch it or look into it unless the Lord gave you authority, no matter what tribe you were, even Levi.
- They got too excited and got nosy, taking a peek to see what the writing of God looked like, and the Lord smote fifty thousand and seventy of them just for peeking. That shows us we have to have a level of discipline over our eyes; with these devices today it is very easy to take a two second look at what you know you should not be looking at. Guard your eyes.
- The people lamented and said, Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God? So they sent messengers to Kirjath-jearim to come fetch the ark up. The Bible acknowledges the Most High God as the king of terrors: he was killing thousands at a time, and his judgments are terrifying.

  Precepts:
  - **[Job 18:14](/bible/job/18#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/job/18#v14)</sup> His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.

    The confidence of the wicked shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors; scripture owns the Most High as the king of terrors.
  - **[Psalms 66:5](/bible/psalms/66#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/psalms/66#v5)</sup> Come and see the works of God: he is terrible in his doing toward the children of men.

    Come and see the works of God: he is terrible in his doing toward the children of men, heathen and wicked Israelite alike.
